subject.title: Gateway process alive but event loop frozen — all HTTP requests silently timeout

question: Should OpenClaw handle process-alive Gateway event-loop freezes by adding systemd WatchdogSec/systemd-notify to generated units, or should this issue stay focused on root-cause removal and diagnostics only?
rationale: The remaining decision changes managed-service behavior and recovery semantics for Linux/systemd users, and the existing candidate PR is conflicting and not live-proven.

options.title: Refresh and prove systemd watchdog
options.body: Adopt the WatchdogSec/systemd-notify direction, require live WSL2 or Linux systemd proof that a wedged event loop stops pings and restarts the Gateway, then close this issue after merge.

options.title: Keep diagnostics/root-cause only
options.body: Reject supervisor auto-restart for now and narrow this issue to the blocking event-loop source plus diagnostic events, leaving recovery to external operator tooling.

options.title: Split recovery from root cause
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical user report, land watchdog recovery under the related PR, and open or link narrower issues for Feishu, memory, provider HTTP, and embedded-run triggers.

recommendation.title: Refresh and prove systemd watchdog
recommendation.body: Adopt the WatchdogSec/systemd-notify direction, require live WSL2 or Linux systemd proof that a wedged event loop stops pings and restarts the Gateway, then close this issue after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and merged the current gateway diagnostics/systemd-unit code in this checkout and is the strongest current-main routing signal.
